title: Exact pairs detecting zero objects detect isomorphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal C,\mathcal D,\mathcal E$ be abelian categories [def-sp-abelian], and let $J:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$ and $I:\mathcal C\to\mathcal E$ be functors preserving zero morphisms, finite limits and finite colimits [def-galois-exact-functor]. A zero object here is an object both initial and terminal. Assume that for every $M\in\mathcal C$, if $JM$ and $IM$ are zero objects, then $M$ is a zero object. For any objects $M,N\in\mathcal C$ and any morphism $c:M\to N$, if $J(c)$ and $I(c)$ are isomorphisms, then $c$ is an isomorphism.
